 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Chicago Bears continued their strong season with a 30-24 victory over the New England Patriots in Week 7 . While the final score suggests a closely contested matchup, two key statistics help explain how Chicago came out on top. From getting off the field on third down to creating explosive plays after the catch, the Bears excelled in critical areas that helped them secure the win.
 Chicago's ability to limit New England's opportunities on offense and generate big plays through the passing game proved decisive. These two statistics highlight how the Bears controlled key moments on both sides of the ball and showed why their offense and defense have helped them emerge as a competitive team this season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Patriots Were Only 2-of-7 on Third Down
 Oct 22, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA;New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (10) is tackled by Chicago Bears linebacker Devin Bush (12) during the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn ImagesMatt Marton-Imagn Images
 It's a cliché, but winning on third down remains one of the biggest factors in football. Chicago consistently got off the field on the money down, forcing the Patriots to stall on five of their seven third-down attempts. In a game that ultimately came down to a one-possession margin, making stops at key moments proved pivotal for the Bears in Week 7. Chicago also forced a turnover on downs on New England's only fourth-down attempt of the night.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement If the Bears hadn't allowed the Patriots' miraculous last-second touchdown at the end of the first half, this statistic would have been even more impressive. Chicago would have entered halftime with a 20-7 lead while holding New England to just one conversion on its first four third-down attempts.
 Bears Produced 163 Yards After the Catch
 Oct 18, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons cornerback Avieon Terrell (12) tackles Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III (10) during the third quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images
 While the Bears' defense consistently got off the field on third down, their offense created explosive plays and gave the unit time to rest. Of Caleb Williams ' 308 passing yards on Thursday night, 163 came after the catch. Luther Burden III accounted for 91 of those yards, including a crucial 58-yard gain that helped spark the Bears' offense early in the game. New England struggled to contain Chicago's pass catchers and their ability to generate yards after the catch.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Those extra yards often made the difference between a short gain and a first down or between a promising drive and a touchdown. Chicago has established itself as a dangerous offense capable of creating big plays after the catch and breaking tackles in the open field. Thursday night's performance showed why that ability makes the Bears one of the NFL's most dangerous offensive teams.
